title: Supreme Court Says California Can Keep Counting Its Ballots
summary:
The Supreme Court has said no to a last-minute request to change how California counts votes.

The midterm elections decide which party controls Congress for the last two years of President Donald Trump's second term. Voting ends on Tuesday, November 3.

The Justice Department asked the court to set aside 20,000 ballots. It said those ballots may have been given to people who are not United States citizens. On Monday, the court answered with a one-line order denying the request. Lower-court rulings will stand, and the effort to disqualify those ballots has essentially ended.

California is the most populous state, with about 23 million people on its voting register. By Sunday night, more than six million mail-in ballots had been received.

Trump and his administration describe a years-long campaign against widespread voter fraud, though research has found such fraud extremely rare.
why_it_matters: When courts decide which ballots count, they help make sure every eligible vote in your state is counted fairly.
